title: Protocol and Debt
premise: August Nystrom, a career interpreter who has survived twelve years of diplomatic service by being indispensable and invisible, is attached to a doomed peace delegation in Geneva when a routine voiceprint authentication accidentally unlocks a black server holding proof that all three negotiating governments have been laundering the war's profits through the very reconstruction fund they are debating. Hunted by an assassin contracted to erase anyone who has heard the recordings, August flees across Europe with Ingrid Sahl, the delegation's idealistic legal adviser, discovering that their own identity was manufactured by the intelligence service they trusted most. As governments close ranks and the assassin closes in, August must choose between returning to the safe anonymity of protocol or burning it all down by broadcasting the truth. The novel ends with August, exposed and stripped of every credential, testifying before a tribunal at personal ruin—while Ingrid chooses to stand beside them, proving that love can outlast duty even when neither survives intact.
about_author: M. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in Geneva, Brussels, and The Hague before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about the people history forgets—the translators, clerks, and couriers who hold secrets no one asked them to carry.

chapters.title: The Glass Booth
chapters.summary: POV August. August interprets the opening session of the Meridian Peace Talks in Geneva, rendering hostile speeches into careful neutrality while noting that both delegations already speak as if failure is scheduled. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking a quiet dread that this mission, like others, is theater.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: POV August. A flashback woven into a sleepless night: how August was recruited young, trained to be unmemorable, and taught that survival means never keeping copies of anything. Emotional beat: melancholy self-erasure; August realizes they cannot remember their mother's voice but remembers every treaty clause.

chapters.title: The Legal Adviser Who Argues
chapters.summary: POV August. August meets Ingrid Sahl, who challenges a procedural ruling the interpreter is required to render verbatim. Their friction crackles; she sees the person inside the function. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination—August hasn't been seen in years.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV August. Asked to verify an archived delegate statement for the record, August's authenticated voiceprint unexpectedly unlocks a hidden partition on the delegation's secure server: audio files implicating all three governments in diverting reconstruction funds. Emotional beat: cold shock hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Recordings Say
chapters.summary: POV August. Over one terrified night, August listens: ministers negotiating casualty figures like commodity prices. One file contains a name—'the Janitor'—and a kill list of potential witnesses. August's own designation appears. Emotional beat: vertigo; invisibility was protection, and it just expired.

chapters.title: Ingrid Reads the Room
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. Ingrid notices August's changed behavior and corners them with lawyer's precision. August, against every instinct, shows her one transcript. Emotional beat: terrifying intimacy—trust as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The First Accident
chapters.summary: POV August. The delegation's archivist, who handled the same server, dies in a hotel stairwell ruled accidental. August recognizes the choreography of a professional cleanup. Emotional beat: grief braided with guilt; the clock is now audible.

chapters.title: Protocol of Flight
chapters.summary: POV August. Using interpreter credentials and a scheduled liaison trip, August smuggles copied drives out of Geneva toward Bern, with Ingrid covering their absence. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear as August breaks rules for the first time.

chapters.title: The Man Who Waits
chapters.summary: POV the assassin (Voss). Introduced through methodical routine: Voss reviews the kill list, notes the archivist complete, and travels to Bern with bureaucratic calm. Emotional beat: chilling ordinariness—evil as punctuality.

chapters.title: Bern, After Hours
chapters.summary: POV August. A dead-drop handoff to a journalist goes wrong; the contact doesn't appear, and August spots surveillance. Ingrid arrives uninvited, forcing improvisation. Emotional beat: panic managed through craft; the two become conspirators in earnest.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. Ingrid maps the legal architecture of the fraud, realizing the tribunal itself is compromised. Her faith in institutions cracks. Emotional beat: disillusionment—the law she loved is the crime's best disguise.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tea
chapters.summary: POV August. The delegation's security chief invites August for tea and asks gentle questions that are not gentle. August performs innocence in three languages. Emotional beat: high-wire tension; lying fluently has never felt so much like dying.

chapters.title: The Janitor's Signature
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Voss cleans up the failed Bern handoff and leaves a deliberate signature—a swept floor—to signal competence upward. We glimpse his employer's chain of command. Emotional beat: dread by implication; the conspiracy is layered and patient.

chapters.title: Night Train South
chapters.summary: POV August and Ingrid alternating. Fleeing on a night train to Lyon, the two share compartment confessions: August's manufactured past, Ingrid's sacrificed marriage to her career. Emotional beat: tenderness under threat—love arriving at the worst possible time.

chapters.title: Safe House That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV August. An old handler offers refuge in Lyon; August discovers the house is wired and the offer is bait to confirm possession of the drives. They escape through back streets. Emotional bet: betrayal by the institution that made them; grief becomes anger.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Personal Edition
chapters.summary: POV August. August burns their real identity documents and adopts a courier legend from an old operation, becoming officially nobody. Emotional beat: liberation and loss intertwined—invisibility reclaimed, but chosen this time.

chapters.title: Marseille Dead Drop
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. Ingrid makes contact with a disgraced ICC investigator, Amara Diallo, trading a sample recording for extraction promises. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the first ally who isn't compromised.

chapters.title: Voss Closes Distance
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Voss identifies the Marseille pattern and requests permission to escalate from witnesses to 'assets.' Permission granted without hesitation. Emotional beat: moral abyss rendered in paperwork; the banality deepens.

chapters.title: The Harbor Mistake
chapters.summary: POV August. A rendezvous at the old port goes loud; Diallo's aide is taken, and August barely pulls Ingrid from a staged arrest. Emotional beat: fury and self-reproach—August's tradecraft saved them but cost someone else.

chapters.title: What August Remembers
chapters.summary: POV August. Under stress, buried memories surface: a childhood village, a recruitment that wasn't voluntary, a family relocated and erased. August's identity was built on someone else's ruins. Emotional beat: shattering recognition—the self was always a cover story.

chapters.title: Ingrid's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. Offered amnesty to walk away and keep her career, Ingrid refuses, formally resigning via encrypted letter that doubles as evidence preservation. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved in duty's own language—she chooses August by choosing the truth.

chapters.title: The Server's Second Lock
chapters.summary: POV August. The drives contain a second encrypted tier requiring a live voiceprint from a specific dead minister—recoverable only from a memorial archive in Vienna. Emotional beat: daunting hope; the truth needs a ghost's voice.

chapters.title: Vienna, City of Treaties
chapters.summary: POV August and Ingrid. Posing as archival researchers, they infiltrate the memorial foundation during a state ceremony. Emotional beat: suspense laced with irony—the machinery of remembrance guards the machinery of lies.

chapters.title: Voice of the Dead
chapters.summary: POV August. August, whose gift is mimicry, must reproduce the minister's cadence to satisfy the biometric lock. It works—but triggers a silent alarm. Emotional beat: triumph inverted into trap; their greatest skill becomes the beacon.

chapters.title: Run Through the Ringstrasse
chapters.summary: POV August. A chase through ceremonial crowds; Voss is meters away, and August recognizes him not by face but by gait. They escape by dissolving into a protest march. Emotional beat: adrenaline and near-recognition—hunter and hunted almost meet eyes.

chapters.title: Amara's Network
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. Diallo reveals a plan: not leaks, which die in news cycles, but a sealed submission to a residual-mandate tribunal with teeth, requiring physical delivery to The Hague within nine days. Emotional beat: strategy replacing flight; purpose crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Delegation Collapses
chapters.summary: POV August. News breaks that the Meridian Talks have failed on schedule; the fraud's architects celebrate publicly. August watches the failure they predicted become cover for everything. Emotional beat: bitter vindication—being right has never mattered less.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Border
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. A trusted member of Diallo's network sells their route; border police detain them in Germany. Ingrid talks them out using procedure as a weapon. Emotional beat: white-knuckle composure; the law still cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Voss's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Reviewing August's file, Voss notices anomalies suggesting his employer orchestrated August's entire life—including this crisis. For the first time, he hesitates. Emotional beat: hairline fracture in the instrument; even tools can wonder.

chapters.title: Amsterdam Interlude
chapters.summary: POV August and Ingrid. One stolen evening in a canal-side room before the final leg. They speak plainly about what happens after—if there is an after. Emotional beat: quiet, mortal tenderness; love stated without hedging for the first time.

chapters.title: The Hague Gates
chapters.summary: POV August. The tribunal's registrar, though sympathetic, cannot accept unsolicited evidence without a sponsoring state—which means walking it into a lion's embassy. Emotional beat: institutional despair; the last door requires the wolves' invitation.

chapters.title: Embassy Gambit
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. Ingrid engineers a scenario where a junior diplomat from a non-signatory state, hungry for leverage, sponsors the submission. Moral compromise acknowledged openly. Emotional beat: pragmatic resolve—clean hands are a luxury the truth can't afford.

chapters.title: Sealed and Filed
chapters.summary: POV August. The evidence enters the tribunal registry under seal. Within hours, the registry clerk who processed it disappears. Emotional beat: grim relief shadowed by cost—victory has a body count.

chapters.title: Voss's Last Contract
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Ordered to eliminate August and Ingrid regardless of the filing, Voss instead delivers his employer's command chain to Diallo and vanishes—or appears to. Emotional beat: the instrument choosing its final note; redemption left deliberately ambiguous.

chapters.title: Hunted Anyway
chapters.summary: POV August. The conspiracy, wounded, retaliates: August and Ingrid are framed as spies, warrants issued across three jurisdictions. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pursuit—the world shrinks to safehouses and borrowed names.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV August. The tribunal grants a closed preliminary hearing. August testifies, voice breaking protocol for the first time—not translating, but speaking as themselves. Emotional beat: catharsis; the interpreter finally interpreted.

chapters.title: Unsealed
chapters.summary: POV Ingrid. The evidence is unsealed; arrests ripple through three capitals. Ingrid watches ministers perp-walked past the same cameras that once broadcast their speeches. Emotional beat: fierce, incomplete justice—the machine corrected, not redeemed.

chapters.title: Cost Accounting
chapters.summary: POV August. The aftermath tallied: careers ended, allies scattered, August's original identity legally confirmed as fabricated—and unrecoverable. Emotional beat: sober reckoning; truth won, but nobody gets their old life back.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Door
chapters.summary: POV August and Ingrid. Standing before a small apartment in a city that asks no questions, they choose new names together rather than apart. Emotional beat: tender resolution—identity rebuilt not as erasure but as authorship.

chapters.title: Protocol and Debt
chapters.summary: POV August, epilogue. Months later, August interprets at a minor trade conference, anonymous again by choice, when a familiar gait passes the booth—Voss, alive, offering the faintest nod. August says nothing, and keeps everything. Emotional beat: earned peace with vigilance; some debts are paid forward, not settled.
